lecture_summary: The lecture develops wave power and intensity, including frequency/amplitude scaling and the inverse-square law; introduces logarithmic sound levels and intensity-to-decibel conversions; and distinguishes moving-source from moving-observer Doppler shifts. Representative problems include doubling speaker distance, converting 60 dB to intensity, combining two equal talkers, and two bat Doppler scenarios.

videos.title: Wave Speed on a String - Tension Force, Intensity, Power, Amplitude, Frequency - Inverse Square Law
videos.reason: Connects power with amplitude and frequency, then covers intensity, distance, and inverse-square reasoning—the foundation for the lecture’s doubled-distance speaker example.

videos.title: Sound Intensity Level in Decibels & Distance - Physics Problems
videos.reason: Directly covers calculating decibels from intensity, recovering intensity from decibels, and relating sound level to distance, matching the lecture’s logarithmic and ratio-based strategies.

videos.title: How To Solve Doppler Effect Physics Problems
videos.reason: Covers moving sources versus moving observers, approaching versus receding motion, and numerical frequency-shift problems, matching the lecture’s equation-selection checklist and bat examples.

coverage_gaps: No playlist description clearly identifies a strong treatment of combining simultaneous sound sources by adding their intensities first, including the important result that doubling intensity raises the level by approximately 3 dB.
